title: Direct image from an open and closed section
statement:
Let $p:V\to X$ be a scheme morphism and
$s:X\hookrightarrow V$ an
open immersion with
closed image and $p s=\operatorname{id}_X$.
For a finite ring $\Lambda$ and
$K\in\hyperref[def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]{D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)}$,
restriction to this component gives a canonical isomorphism

$$
Rp_*s_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}K,
$$

where $Rp_*$ and $s_!$ are the
derived direct image and
extension by zero.

proof.text: Put $U=s(X)$ and $Z=V\setminus U$, both open subschemes. The open immersion identifies $X$ with $U$, and the two inclusions exhibit $V=U\amalg Z$: morphisms from the two disjoint opens glue uniquely, with no overlap conditions. Apply the finite clopen coproduct equivalence to abelian etale sheaves. It also gives an equivalence for $\Lambda$-module sheaves: a $\Lambda$-action is a family of abelian-sheaf endomorphisms indexed by $\Lambda$ satisfying the ring identities; these endomorphisms and their identities are recovered componentwise by the fully faithful equivalence. Thus $\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)\simeq\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\times\Mod(Z_{\Et},\Lambda)$, with restriction to $X$ the first projection.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: disjoint open cover and sheaf gluing; Stacks 0A5B (etale-cohomology-lemma-constant-smooth-statements), first proof paragraph

proof.text: Under this equivalence $s_!$ is $(F,0)$. Indeed $(F,0)$ is left adjoint to first projection, since $\Hom((F,0),(G,H))=\Hom(F,G)$, and extension by zero is left adjoint to restriction; uniqueness of a left adjoint identifies them canonically. The same insertion is right adjoint to first projection since $\Hom((G,H),(F,0))=\Hom(G,F)$. First projection is exact: kernels and cokernels in a product abelian category are the pairs of component kernels and cokernels. The right-adjoint injectivity lemma therefore shows that $s_!$ preserves injectives. Its exactness also ensures its degreewise functor acts on derived categories.

source.place: Proof, sentences 2-3: extension by zero and injective preservation; Stacks 03DI (sites-modules-lemma-extension-by-zero), 03DJ (sites-modules-lemma-extension-by-zero-exact), 015Z (homology-lemma-adjoint-preserve-injectives)

proof.text: For each etale $W\to X$, set $T=V\times_X W$. The projection $q:T\to V$ is etale, being the base change of $W\to X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], the underlying abelian sheaf $G=(s_!F)|_T$ has $G(T)=(s_!F)(T)$ and $G(A\to T)=(s_!F)(A\to V)$ for each etale $A\to T$. These identifications also respect each scalar endomorphism, hence the $\Lambda$-module structures. The complementary opens of $T$ are $U\times_XW\cong W$ (using $ps=\mathrm{id}_X$) and $Z\times_XW$. Restricting the component sheaf $(F,0)$ to these opens gives $(F|_W,0)$; this follows directly by restricting the componentwise reconstruction, and respects its $\Lambda$-action. The global-sections clause of the clopen coproduct lemma, applied to $G$ on $T$, gives $(p_*s_!F)(W)=(s_!F)(T)\cong F(W)\times0\cong F(W)$ as $\Lambda$-modules. The map is restriction to the first component. For a map $W'\to W$ both composites restrict to $W'$, and for a sheaf map $F\to F'$ both composites apply that map to the restricted section. Hence these identifications form a natural sheaf isomorphism $p_*s_!\cong\mathrm{id}$, rather than only objectwise equalities.

source.place: Proof, displayed section identity: direct image evaluated on an etale test scheme; Stacks 0A5B first proof paragraph for component sections; Stacks 03S2 (section-extension-by-zero), paragraph after Definition 03S3, etale inverse image as restriction

proof.text: The module-sheaf categories on $X$ and $V$ have enough injectives. Choose a bounded below complex $I$ of injective $\Lambda$-module sheaves and an isomorphism $QI\cong K$, using the $D^+$ representative lemma. It is K-injective. By step 2, $s_!I$ is again bounded below with injective terms, hence is K-injective by the same lemma and represents $s_!K$. Applying the computation-on-injectives clause of the right-derived-functor lemma to $p_*$ gives $Rp_*s_!K\cong Q(p_*s_!I)$. Step 3 in every degree commutes with differentials by naturality in sheaf maps, so it is a chain isomorphism $p_*s_!I\cong I$. Thus $Rp_*s_!K\cong QI\cong K$.

source.place: Proof, last two sentences: bounded-below injective resolution; Stacks 013K (lemma-injective-resolutions-exist), 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective), 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic), 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived)

proof.text: Let $r_I:p_*s_!I\to I$ be the chain isomorphism of step 3 and $\alpha_{s_!I}:Q(p_*s_!I)\to Rp_*Q(s_!I)$ the derived comparison. On this representative the asserted map is $\tau_I=Q(r_I)\alpha_{s_!I}^{-1}:Rp_*Q(s_!I)\to QI$. For a derived morphism $f:K\to K'$ choose identifications $QI\cong K$, $QI'\cong K'$; the K-injective Hom bijection represents $f$ by a unique homotopy class $h:I\to I'$. Step 3 gives $r_{I'}(p_*s_!h)=h r_I$, while naturality of the comparison gives $Rp_*Q(s_!h)\alpha_{s_!I}=\alpha_{s_!I'}Q(p_*s_!h)$. Inverting the comparisons and combining these equations gives $\tau_{I'}Rp_*Q(s_!h)=Q(h)\tau_I$, proving naturality after the chosen identifications. For a second representative $J$ of the same $K$, the Hom bijection lifts the induced isomorphism $QI\to QJ$ and its inverse to $h:I\to J$ and $g:J\to I$; injectivity of that bijection gives $gh=\mathrm{id}_I$ and $hg=\mathrm{id}_J$ in the homotopy category. Thus $h$ is a homotopy equivalence. Substituting this $h$ into the two displayed compatibility equations shows that the two maps to $K$ agree after the representative identifications. The resulting isomorphism is therefore independent of the representative and is precisely restriction to the section component.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: identity in each degree gives the asserted derived isomorphism; Stacks 070I (lemma-K-injective), 05SA (lemma-derived-functor)
